(•̀ᴗ•́) Review report: te-c2tc

Checkout matched `/Users/alexispurslane/.t3/worktrees/bookfin/t3-dac305e5`, branch `t3/stabilize-epub-builder-timestamps`. Reviewed the complete diff from `5c8c92ecd348a7fb7c51ab176da6e616cfd2aa1c` to `60115c14377f6397decff61e4e73ce35f575314a`. Status was clean before and after review.

Read the required instructions, plan, ticket, reviewer guidance, and software-design skill. No `CLAUDE.md` was present. No files changed, tests ran, builds ran, formatting or analysis commands ran, or delegates started. Results below come from read-only source inspection and retained execution evidence.

1. Correctness/regressions — pass

   All seven fixture owners receive the fixed local-calendar entry time. Contents, entry order, fixture interfaces, missing-entry cases, and deliberate CRC damage remain intact. The CSS rewrite changes timestamps only for replacement CSS entries. Both showcase wrapper overrides and their named identities remain unchanged.

   The archived diagnostic exercises the real builders independently with supplied clock times two seconds apart. Its dependency patch changes only the lazy default timestamp, plus the necessary import. Retained output confirms eight passing checks and seven expected stability failures before correction, then all 15 checks passing afterward. All seven changed-content identity checks pass. Payload hashes and entry order match across both phases.

   The `pages.book` evidence correctly distinguishes its raw archive digest from its admitted text entries. The prior t3-5o5r logs substantiate the restart failure after a completed save when timestamps differ, and successful restoration when timestamps match. They do not establish historical scheduling.

   Git object comparisons confirm unchanged production code, dependencies, assets, shared publication/session helpers, and the original restart test. Retained focused/full logs show the restart assertion, changed-content rejection, and named showcase identity checks passing.

   Findings: no implementation defects found. Gaps: optional downloaded-book and benchmark paths remain gated; those are not claimed passes.

2. Ticket fulfillment — pass, with one nonblocking documentation finding

   The settled seven-owner scope is complete. Independent inspection reproduces the 89-file transitive caller set. Additional research creators are recorded in `td-bz4y`; no unrelated implementation or asset regeneration entered the diff.

   All 45 manifest entries and all 27 compressed archives match their recorded hashes. The Dart patch retained for every final check exactly matches HEAD: SHA-256 `58478615bb990dcec17f257374d207c9e035b7864a81e5d6c9b52d88c2233e7b`. Current package configuration and shared dependency bytes match their saved originals; temporary diagnostic access is absent.

   Retained execution results:

   | Check | Passed | Skipped | Failed |
   |---|---:|---:|---:|
   | Focused | 99 | 8 | 0 |
   | Affected callers | 1,195 | 18 | 0 |
   | Full suite | 3,768 | 27 | 0 |

   Commands record Nix execution, Flutter concurrency two, and sequential heavy runs. Retained analysis reports no issues; formatting reports zero changes; the final whitespace check exits successfully. Both resolved development problems are documented.

   Finding F1 — low severity, nonblocking: [inventory.json:89](/Users/alexispurslane/.t3/worktrees/bookfin/t3-dac305e5/docs/evidence/te-c2tc/inventory.json:89) incorrectly says the navigator raster-fallback probes retain original `ZipInfo` metadata.

   Exact evidence from [test_raster_fallback.py:47](/Users/alexispurslane/.t3/worktrees/bookfin/t3-dac305e5/tool/research/readers/navigator/test_raster_fallback.py:47):

   ```python
                        changed.writestr(SVG, content)
   ```

   where

   - `changed` is the new in-memory ZIP archive.
   - `writestr` writes an archive entry from a name and contents.
   - `SVG` is the entry’s filename string.
   - `content` is the modified SVG text.

   Trigger: consulting the inventory to classify timestamp-dependent writers. Impact: inaccurate audit rationale, without affecting the seven-owner correction. Remedy: describe these as SVG/JPEG resource probes that create fresh entries but do not build EPUB publications. Update the manifest hash if the evidence file changes.

   No material acceptance requirement remains unverified.

3. Design — pass

   The correction follows the existing fixture-owner model. Callers retain the same interfaces and need no timestamp knowledge. No shared mutable state, cached book copies, public clock options, production exceptions, or generic framework were introduced.

   Under User/Ousterhout ownership rules, fixture construction remains responsible for reproducible fixture metadata, while production retains source-identity enforcement. Under Muratori’s guidance, these short independent assignments do not justify a new abstraction. Fixture-content changes remain local; no new coordinated caller edits are required.

   Findings: no concrete ownership, information-leakage, or change-amplification defect found. Gaps: no material design requirement remains unverified.

Overall verdict: pass, with F1 as a nonblocking evidence correction.

Unavailable checks: fresh execution was prohibited. Existing gated downloads, benchmarks, and live integration checks were not exercised by this review. Device acceptance, coverage, mutation testing, integration, and closure remain parent-owned.
